title: Optimize pager suppression and alert fidelity after capacity-induced SLO breach
creator: Maria Gonzales
description:
Summary: During a capacity pressure event on 2026-02-08 we observed a sustained SLO breach for text-generation endpoints leading to noisy paging and duplicated incident work across oncall. Root cause was an interaction between autoscaler cooldown settings and a new kernel scheduling optimization that raised tail latency under degraded GPU packing. Several burn-rate alerts fired rapidly and were configured to page immediately, which amplified noise and caused operator fatigue.

Goals: 1) Reduce actionable pages by suppressing duplicates and tuning burn-rate thresholds without degrading detection of customer-visible outages. 2) Improve alert fidelity by mapping signals to runbooks and ensuring alerts include sufficient context (model variant, region, percent SLO burn, recent scaling events). 3) Prevent regression by adding automated tests for alert thresholds and a canary that simulates capacity churn.

Scope: Backend alert rules (burn-rate, p50/p95 tail latency paging rules), oncall routing and suppression windows, observability payload enrichment, and unit/e2e tests that assert alert behavior under synthetic load patterns.
action_items: Audit current burn-rate alert rules and add a 15-minute aggregated suppression window to avoid duplicate pages for the same customer-request-group (owned by SRE)
Introduce a secondary 'escalation only' burn-rate threshold (higher % burn) that will page; keep lower threshold for dashboarding and Slack alerts only (owner: runtime infra)
Add contextual metadata to alerts: model_variant, region, autoscaler_status, recent_deploy_id and recent_kernel-optimization-flag (owner: telemetry team)
Adjust autoscaler cooldown from 120s to 240s for GPU pools handling large-context models to avoid oscillation during transient pressure (owner: capacity team), monitor for 2 weeks
Roll back the scheduling optimization behind a feature flag on low-priority pools and run A/B to measure tail latency impact under constrained packing (owner: runtime-performance)
Create a 'synthetic churn' test harness that generates realistic KV cache warmup + variable batch sizes to validate alert thresholds in CI (owner: qa-infra)
Add a pager playbook with step-by-step triage and a decision matrix for paging vs Slack (owner: SRE and oncall leads)
Add an automatic suppression that groups sequential burn alerts by contributing region and model for 30 minutes (owner: alerting platform)
Schedule a follow-up review in two weeks to iterate thresholds based on real incidents and remove temporary escalations once stable (owner: PM)
Link the postmortem and action-items to a GitHub PR that implements the alert change and to a dashboard that shows before/after paging metrics (owner: assignee)
Document risk and rollback criteria for each change in the change-log and include an emergency rollback runbook (owner: security/compliance)
Create metric-level SLO guard rails that will auto-mute non-customer-impacting signals for 48 hours when a global capacity incident is declared (owner: platform ops)
